# [Baseline] - AND - D - Compliance Dedicated Device Health

Marks a dedicated Android device (kiosk or shared) as non-compliant when it is rooted, Play Integrity does not pass with hardware backing, the Intune app has been tampered with, storage is not encrypted or the latest security patch is older than the minimum.

| | |
|---|---|
| Platform | Android |
| Scope | Device (D) — assign to device groups |
| Type | Compliance |
| Assignment | — |
| Source | UniFy Android Enterprise Baseline v1.5.1 — AND - CP - DEV - Corp-Dedicated - Kiosk and Shared - v1.5; without password and OS version requirements, patch level added |
| File | [`Baseline_AND_D_Compliance_Dedicated_Device_Health.json`](Baseline_AND_D_Compliance_Dedicated_Device_Health.json) |

> Deliberately no device code: a single-app kiosk often has none, and on a shared device Managed Home Screen handles the session PIN. Deliberately no OS minimum: rugged devices (scanners, tills) stay on an older major version for a long time but still receive patches from the manufacturer — the patch date (2026-03-01) is the honest measure there. Before assigning, check whether the fleet passes hardware attestation; old kiosk hardware sometimes fails it immediately (UniFy W-18). In addition, devices in Entra shared device mode do not receive the user policies of whoever is signed in — on dedicated devices Intune applies only device assignments.

## Properties — 28

A compliance policy has no settingDefinitionIds but fixed properties. `scheduledActionsForRule` determines what happens when a device does not comply.
